utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And how old were you when you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to read and review this statement in preparation for your appearance here today?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I understand that you made some corrections and clarifications to the statement after reviewing it for the preparation of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And these corrections are in paragraph 1 of both statements. It's e-court number -- e-court page 1 -- 2 for the English version. You were ten years old. It states in paragraph 1 that you were 10 years old but it should be nine years old?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And when you say that -- in paragraph 2, when you say that you lived in an area across from the TV station, you didn't mean literally across from the TV station.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And in paragraph 4 of the statement, when you say that you went to wooded hills near the front lines with your father, you didn't actually go near the front lines but that your perception, as a child, made you believe that the front lines appeared to be closer than they actually were.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And in paragraph 7, you say -- when you say the shrapnel went through, it should be that the shrapnel went through your left hand and your right cheek?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And finally in paragraph 9 of the statement where you mention the other side of the building from a sort of military headquarters, the building was not actually directly behind this headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Okay. And now other than the corrections made to the statement, if you were asked today the same questions that you were asked when you -- when you gave this statement, would you give the same answers and provide the same information, in substance?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the truthfulness and the accuracy of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would like to tender this witness's -- this witness statement dated February 12, 2000, with paragraphs hand numbered by the Office of the Prosecutor bearing 65 ter 28447 as the next public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I received a sign by Mr. Stojanovic that there is no objection. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28447 becomes Exhibit P415, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P415 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now summarise this witness's written evidence for the record. Muhamed Kapetanovic is a witness to scheduled shelling incident G6 which occurred on the 22nd January, 1994. The witness was nine years old and living in a 16-storey apartment building in Sarajevo. On the date of the incident, at around noon, the witness had gone outside to play in the snow with his -- with four of his friends. As they were sledding in front of their apartment building, they heard a sound of a shell exploding nearby and began running towards their building. A shell landed behind them which injured Mr. Kapetanovic and two of his friends. One of Mr. Kapetanovic's friends was decapitated by the shell. The witness was injured on his right cheek, his left leg and left hand as a result of the shelling. He was taken to Dobrinja hospital with his father, where he received first aid care. He was subsequently taken to Kosevo hospital where he spent one and a half months for further treatment. Following this incident, the witness spent two years in Italy receiving further medical treatment as a result of his injures from the shelling, including seven operations. This concludes my summary for the witness's written evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Lee. If you would have further questions, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic in which neighbourhood in Sarajevo did you live in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And was the name of your street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Cetinska, number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And do you currently live in the same neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Do you still live in the same apartment?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And has the street name changed since January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It has been renamed into Getes Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And do you know when this name was changed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Now, do you know a street called Clara Zetkin Street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And where is Clara Zetkin Street located in relation to Cetinska Street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And when you say "in the immediate vicinity," do you mean that there is an intersection or -- can you elaborate on what you meant by "the immediate vicinity?"

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Cetinska Street, the part of the neighbourhood where I live, is in that general area. Clara Zetkin Street and Cetinska street start roughly on the same spot but they diverge into opposite directions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: So if you are on Cetinska Street walking towards -- are you also on Clara Zetkin Street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Okay. So then am I correct to understand that Cetinska Street is a continuation of Clara Zetkin Street? It's the same street that turns into a different name.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And has Clara Zetkin Street also changed its name since January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: What is it called today?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Bosanska Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, for your reference I refer you to page 32 of the hard copy of Exhibit 3, and it's page 37 in e-court. And this is a -- sorry, the court binder. It is a map of the neighbourhood containing both Gotijeva [phoen] Street and Bosanka Street that the witness has just mentioned. And because of time constraint, I will not go to that map.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I'm now going to show you a 360-degree photograph which was taken in 2002, and after showing you this photograph, I will ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, Ms. Stewart will now bring 65 ter 10275B to our screens. It's a quick time video illustrating a 360-degree panoramic ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you recognise the street and its surrounding?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And the street that we're looking at now, what is the name of the street shown in this photo?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Cetinska.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And if you were standing on the street facing the green shed here, which direction would you be facing?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The north.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Okay. And now, looking at this street and its surrounding, how does it compare to the way you remembered it in January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Do -- do the street, the buildings around it, were these buildings already existent in January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And do you see any substantive change in the neighbourhood from what you've seen in this panoramic video compared to the way you had remembered this neighbourhood in January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In the main, everything is the same. Except for the green house, I'm not sure that it was there before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Okay. And, now, I'll take you back to January of 1994 during the war. Did you go out to play often with your friends?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever it was calm, we would go out.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And when you say "calm," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: There was no shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 5 of your statement, you say that you and your friends were sledding on a little slope in front of your building. Now, when you look at this green shed on this picture, can you remember in relation to that building where you were playing with your friends on January 22nd, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was close to the green house, although I don't remember if the house was there at the time at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember the names of the friends that you were playing with that day?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And can you spell their names for the record.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Danijel Juranic, Admir Ahmethodzic and Elvir Ahmethodzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And at paragraph 6 of your statement, when you state that you heard a loud explosion and you started to run, do you remember how many explosions you heard before you began to run?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: One or two. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We heard an explosions and started running in the direction of our entrance way. One shell landed behind us. Danijel Juranic was hit, whereas Admir, Elvir and I were seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And when said Danijel was hit, did you see him get hit?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was right behind me. And as I turned around I saw that his head had been severed from the body by shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And do you know how old Danijel was at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: He was my senior by one or two years. So he may have been 10 or 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier that Admir and Elvir were also injured. Do you know how old they were?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Elvir was the oldest among us. I think he was roughly four years older than me. And Admir, roughly two years older than me.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: So, now you're running, you're all running towards the building, and you fall on the ground. Do you remember what happened next?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I fell. I tried to get up. I couldn't. I fell to the ground again and saw that my leg was injured. As I fell down, I turned around and saw Danijel lying headless. My father arrived at that point. Some persons came with a car and picked us up, the three of us, in a group who were injured there. I myself was taken to the Dobrinja hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I would like to tender this 360-degree photograph bearing 65 ter 10275B as the next public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Ms. Lee, you asked the witness a few questions about a specific portion of this 360-degree panoramic video and I'd like to put on the record where we looked at when you asked these questions. The questions you asked after, where the transcript says "video-clip played," we are then looking at that portion of the video which shows a street, and to the left a little white van at a distance, some people standing before it, and on the right, a person walking on the pavement, more or less behind what seems to be a traffic sign, and in the back of it, a light green structure with a brown belt on it. That was the portion we looked at when you asked these questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's hereby put on the record. Any objections against admission? Yes. But let's first deal with the -- Mr. Stojanovic, any objection against admission of the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as a matter of principle I do not, but you think it would be fair for the transcript to say when this photo was taken, especially in view of what the witness has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, first of all, admission, no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10275B becomes Exhibit P416, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Any information as to when the photograph was taken, Ms. Lee?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I have prefaced to the witness before playing that and this photograph was taken in 2002. The exact date is 28th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Judge Moloto has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, good morning. I just want to ask one question. Are you able, looking at this picture, to show us the building which houses your apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The only thing that shows is the grey building in the upper right corner. That's number 5. And the entrance to where our apartment is, is behind this.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I play -- can I show him the entire 360 and perhaps the witness could point out whether or not he recognises his apartment building. Because right now we're only looking at one clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you move it slightly, I take it then, to the right. And let's do it in steps of 45 degrees approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And also for your information, Your Honour, I am --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is approximately 45 degrees, I would say, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I will also be tendering still images of this panoramic photo which I will be dealing very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, now looking at this picture again, could you further explain your previous answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to move -- pan out a little further. This is the building where I live, but not the right entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are now looking at a picture -- a part of the picture where the word "foto" on the building is to the very right. We'll now pan further for another 45 degrees. Could we stop here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we see entrance number 3, and our apartment is at the next entrance, number 2. So we have to rotate a bit further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we looked at is now the building central in the picture where the word "foto" still appears, approximately 90 degrees, which would mean east, direction east, compared to where we started with north. Could we pan further another 45 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's 45 degrees approximately. A little bit beyond that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you can see our entrance, approximately where the man walking on the pavement can be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Lee.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, were you shown still pictures of this 360-photograph in preparation of your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I please ask the Court Officer to bring 65 ter 10275A to our screens and these are the three still images taken from P416. And could I also please have the usher's assistance in setting up the smart monitor so that the witness could mark on these images in red. Your Honours, I will be asking the witness to make several markings. Would this time be more appropriate to take a break or should we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you inform us as to how much time you would still need.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I would need about 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because your initial assessment was --

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 45 minutes. Okay, I think it would be better to take a break first. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We take a short break, Mr. Kapetanovic, and then we'd like to see you back. Would you please follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait for the witness to appear, Ms. Lee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Lee, you may proceed with your examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Is the Smart monitor on for the witness marking in red?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can I ask that you not make any markings until you have finished listening to my question and also until I ask you to mark the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can we go to e-court page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Looking at this picture, can you tell us where the shell that had injured you and your friends fell?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This photo is taken, actually, from the spot where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Now, can you see on this picture the location where you and your friends were sledding that day?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Please mark it with an X and put number 1 beside it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Could you indicate with an arrow the direction toward which you and your friends were running after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. We were running towards the entrance to our apartment building.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like it tender this picture as marked by the witness as the next public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10275A, as marked by the witness, becomes Exhibit P417, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. The witness used a circle rather than an X to make his first marking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 2 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you see your building in this picture?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can you mark it with an X and put number 2 beside it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The entrance itself is not shown in this picture. This is entrance number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Okay. But you see your building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And can you mark your building.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And put number 2 beside it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can you see on this picture the location where you were thrown to the ground after the shelling?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Please mark it with an X and put number 3 beside it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Do you see the location where you saw Danijel's body after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I'd like you to put an X and put number 4 beside it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Danijel was right behind me, here.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And could you also indicate with an arrow the direction towards which you and your friends were running after hearing the loud explosion.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this picture as marked by the witness as the next public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P418, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we understand that these -- this -- this is the -- this was the second page of the 65 ter number you indicated at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it now receives a separate exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Exhibit number. Because it has different markings, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can we now go to page three in e-court of the same 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you see -- first of all, what street are we on here?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Cetinska Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And can you see Clara Zetkin Street on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Now can you draw a line where Cetinska Street ends and where Clara Zetkin Street begins?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately about here is where Cetinska ends, and then Clara Zetkin begins. And towards us, that's where Cetinska Street is.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: So now I see that you made an arrow and that's towards Clara Zetkin Street. That would be -- where the arrow is, that you would be on Clara Zetkin Street there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can you -- I apologise. Can you put a K beside it, beside the arrow.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can you see on this picture the location where you fell on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Please put an X on it and put number 5 beside it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And can you see where Admir fell after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I would like to -- I apologise. I would like you to put an X and put number 6 beside it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Lee, the Chamber wonders whether it is really necessary on the second photograph where we see more or less the same to mark again what -- the whole marking, of course, the relevance of that is already subject to some doubt, but in view of the adjudicated facts. But then to have it marked on two photographs -- okay. But let's proceed --

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes, that was my last marking, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your last marking. Then, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 3 of document 10275A as marked by witness becomes Exhibit P419, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you know how many people were injured or killed by the shelling on the 22nd of January, 1994, along with you and your friends.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Six children were killed. There were three who were wounded in my group, and that is in Cetinska Street; whereas in Clara Zetkin, I'm not exactly sure about the number of boys who were injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, in paragraph 9 of your statement, you say that the spot where you and your friends were sledding was on the other side of the building from some sort of military headquarters. Could you tell us who you believed occupied this sort of military headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, their name was Kulin Ban.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, in reliance of adjudicated fact 2434, I will move on from this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I will now play a video of a news broad from the 22nd of January, 1994. After playing this video I will have some specific questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Stewart will now play the video-clip bearing 65 ter 28448, using Sanction. Your Honour, I take it that the protocol is to play the video twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to rely on the text, then it should be played twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And the transcripts have been provided to the booths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before it will be played again, one second, Ms. Lee. Mr. Kapetanovic, I can imagine that it's not easy for you to look at these pictures. Now, for very technical reasons, we have to play it again, but if you would prefer not to see it for a second time at this moment, I'll ask your monitor to be switched off when we look at it for a second time, and if you would prefer to take your earphones off, you're free to do so. I just wanted to inquire with you, whether you'd prefer not to look a second time within ten minutes to this. Would you prefer not to look at it again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will look at it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will play it again and that's mainly for us to receive the proper translation. That's the reason why we play it place.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I will be stopping at various segments of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And I would like the witness to comment. Can I stop at those segments at this time or should we play the entire clip again and then go back to those?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can stop. But then have you to wait until the translation, up to that point in time, is finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then can you ask questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover]: Today on this spot in Sarajevo six boys and girls were killed by two criminal shells. Two were seriously injured. Six young Sarajevans were killed in the name of the insane cause of a Greater Serbia. Their only fault was that they trusted the deceptive calm. Not one of the victim boys and girls had been born yet at the time of the winter Olympics in Sarajevo exactly 10 years ago. The little Olympians exchanged their occupied ice ranges and sleighing slopes on the surrounding hills for the ice on the parking lot. On these sleds two girls got killed. They had borrowed the sleds from their friends."

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you recognise this street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have just stopped at 56 seconds of the video. Can we now please continue to play.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover]: The majority of the Bosnian people cannot receive the signal of Bosnia and Herzegovina television. This broadcast is rebroadcast on the radio and therefore we will relate that. Right now on the screen there are imagines of scattered brain matter and blood sled by Sarajevo boys and girls. Our radio signal can be heard in Serbia. Tonight Serbia should hear that her heros killed six little Sarajevans with their cannons today. Serbia must hear that so far her sons have killed other 1.600 Sarajevo children and about 20.000 in Bosnia Herzegovina. Serbia should hear that these were not only Muslim children. Here, Serbian soldiers are also killing Serbian and Croatian children and children from mixed marriages. Today and tomorrow are days of rest in Serbia and Europe. Belgrade TV will not broadcast the images of the dead little Sarajevans. The European TV stations will edit out these horrific images in order not to spoil the weekend for the viewers. The diplomatics come of Europe and the world are skiing with their children on the mountain slopes of Europe. The children in Serbia and Europe today..."

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have stopped at 2 minutes and 8 seconds within the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this location is in relation to where you fell?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This is Cetinska Street and further on it's Clara Zetkin Street. While I was back, further back.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: We could continue playing this video.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover]: The children in Serbia and Europe today do not know that their fathers are criminals. We are poorer today for six little lilies. We're six times sadder today than we were yesterday. Today we have to be six times stronger. "These chilling imagines of massacred children's bodies are proof of the hell of war that we're going through. Today, again, from the surrounding hills the Chetniks continued killing and destroying everything that is human and worth mentioning. Chetniks shells have forever ended the lives of six of our youngest citizens. All they were guilty of was sledding. "The seriously injured 10-year-old ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have stopped at 3 minutes and 7 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, who is this person?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover]: The seriously injured Muhamed Kapetanovic was taken to hospital by his father. Four shells fell on Alipasino Polje block C in Cetinska street and Clara Zetkin Street. At that moment I was in the bathroom. The little one was outside" --

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: We have stopped at 3 minutes and 16 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic who is this person?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That is my father.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Hamed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: His full name?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Hamed Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover]: At that moment, I was in the bathroom. The little one was outside and when my daughters looked out the window they screamed saying, The little one is getting killed. I ran out, barely managing to put on some clothes. I didn't even dry myself off. When I came down they were lying there. There were many dead and injured. First aid was administered at Dobrinja and now I brought him here and I don't know what will be with him. He is seriously injured. Muhamed was seriously injured in the jaw and leg by a shell. "We were by the sheds skating. All of a sudden a shell fell. We started running. In front of us we started running towards the house entrance and as Danijel and I started running, a shell landed between the two of us. He was killed on the spot and I was injured in four places. The doctors are still fighting for the lives of the brothers, Ahmethodzic, Elvir and Admir.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, at the end of the video, the reporter mentioned two names, Elvir and Admir. Are these the same two friends with whom you were playing that day?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And, finally, Mr. Kapetanovic, do you know the extent of the injures that Admir and Elvir sustained from the shelling?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Admir's left leg was amputated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat what he said last.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you repeat your answer. I think the interpreters have not heard you fully. Can you repeat if you know the extent of injuries that Admir and Elvir sustained.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Admir's left leg was amputated below the hip. And Elvir had also sustained injured to his left leg.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And how do you know this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Do you -- are you still -- did you remain in contact with them?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would like it tender into evidence the video-clip as the next public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I have just the number of the video-clip?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it's 65 ter 28448. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P420, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, this completes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Lee. Mr. Stojanovic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be short, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Miodrag Stojanovic, and I am one the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to tell Mr. Kapetanovic that you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic, who introduced himself already as a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have document P3 in e-court, the photograph on page 5. While we're waiting for it, Your Honours, it's a collection of photographs provided by the Prosecution which were used repeatedly in the courtroom before. Can we zoom in on the lower part of the photograph, the centre. It's an aerial image.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, kindly tell us if you can by looking at the airport runway find the location of the buildings that you spoke of earlier.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't see them at the moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then look at page 6 of the same document. We'll come back to this image later. Thank you. Let us enlarge the central area where we have the green and red frames. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, by looking at this photograph, can you find the areas that you marked on the previous photographs?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark, the same way as you did before, with a red circle, the spot where you were at the time the shell was fired?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The photograph is rather small.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Lee.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was just wondering since this witness has made markings in red for the Prosecution, if the markings could be done in a different colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is usually done. It's now marking -- at the request of the Defence will be in blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could the photograph, could it be blown up a bit, to say the lower left part to be blown up. Does this help you, Mr. Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then mark with a circle the places you were asked to do, the spot where you were at the time the shell was fired. And I take it, Mr. Stojanovic, that you intend to ask the witness to mark the spot when the shell was fired that hit the witness or any of the previous shells he heard being fired?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. I will have other questions, and we will be marking spot by spot. And we will use it as one exhibit ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So the first question was to mark the spot where you were at the time when the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: So you mean where I stood? Well, roughly here. I am not that precise, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you make it a circle and mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this same map, if you recall, can you mark the spot where, to the best of your knowledge, the first shell landed which prompted you to start running?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where the first shell landed. We only heard the sound and started running.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And thirdly, can you mark the spot where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Lee.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. The witness just made the marking after hearing the first question and he was asked to put a circle and put a place number 1 beside it. And I just see two little circles and so if that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the two little circles you have drawn are approximately indicating where you were when the shell fell which hit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The place that I marked was the place where I was when I heard the first explosion. And if you could blow up the image further, it will be clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to ask the technical service to do that, although then we will lose the markings. So I will ask the witness to mark the places again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we somewhere again have on the screen the same picture and not store the markings as we had them now and then to blow up the central part. Still a bit more, please. Are you able to orient yourself, Mr. Kapetanovic, on the -- on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you mark again with a little circle and a number 1 where you were when you heard the shells being fired, when you were still playing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you now also mark where you were when the shell landed which hit you? Also a circle and please a little 2 perhaps to the right of that circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The upper circle was the circle marked by number 1. The lower one by number 2. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to place the circle and number 3 at the location where, to the best of your recollection, the command of the Kulin Ban BH army unit was located?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Objection. I object to this question, Your Honour. Information was put to the witness that it was a command of a BiH army, and that's something that this witness has not testified to anywhere. So that's suggesting -- it is rather suggestive, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But it is clear to you, you referred to Kulin Ban. That's the name you thought was given to a certain location. Could you mark with a circle -- you've done it already. I see it. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not want to interrupt my questioning, but I would like to present to you item 9 which is adduced here as evidence where the witness said that the place where we were skating was across from the location where there was some sort of military staff. So when I said staff I was referring to what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter -- the matter has been resolved. So let's not -- let's proceed at this moment and elicit further evidence from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I apologise, but I will have several short questions. Don't hold it against me. To the best of your recollection, how long was it between the first and the second shells landed? How much time elapsed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My second question. Can you give us an estimation of the distance you covered, or of the distance between the place you stood when you heard the first shell land and which you marked as circle number 1 and the place that you marked where you were hit?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly 10 to 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So am I right in saying that the -- in the time interval between the two shells, you covered these 10 to 15 metres? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: When the first shell landed, we started running, and then the second landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your help. At the time, you didn't know what sort of shell it was and what weapon fired it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't even know the direction the shell flew in from.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know who it was who fired the shell, do you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I am sorry for everything that happened to you, and I have no other questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, if this is the right time, I would suggest that we do as we did before, which is that the witness should sign the marked photographs so that we can tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we never did that here. And the markings are clear in e-court, so, therefore, there's no need to do that. Madam Registrar, the number of this marked map would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Of the page 5 of document P3 as marked by the witness in court will become Exhibit D82, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. It is admitted into evidence. Any need for further investigation -- further examination, Ms. Lee?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, in light of the cross-examination, I have a couple of --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. I apologise to my learned friend. If I was told correctly, this is page 6 rather than page 5 of the collection of the aerial images. I want to avoid any confusion. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most important is we know what we're looking at. Madam Registrar has managed to get this on the screen and that the exhibit, as now admitted, reflects whatever page it was, the cut-out portion of the map as it's found in the binders. I even think that the page number is page --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is page 6, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's page 6. And it's -- in the hard copy version it is page 3, a cut-out of page 3. Yes. Ms. Lee.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, the Kulin Ban that you mentioned and that you marked here as number 3, this building, have you ever visited this building during the war?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't. But I was close by.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And did you know the Kulin Ban personally?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: So do you know which -- to which army the Kulin Ban belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I'm -- did you know -- did you know personally at that time which -- which army that the Kulin Ban belonged to? Is this something that you knew from your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did know that. They bore the insignia of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: And my final question is: On the day before hearing the first shell that landed in the vicinity where you and your friends were playing, did you hear any shells or gun-fires that came out of your neighbourhood or near the Kulin Ban building on the date of the incident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no speaking. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that the question does not arise from cross-examination. It actually is beyond the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Well, Kulin Ban was specifically addressed by you, so, therefore, it is so closely related to what was asked in cross-examination that Ms. Lee may put this question. Could you please repeat the question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, on the date of the incident, before hearing the first shell and after which you -- you and your friends began to run home, did you hear -- or did you -- did you hear any shells or gun-fires that came from your neighbourhood or this Kulin Ban building that you just marked?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear any explosions. That day was peaceful, and that was why we were outdoors.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, this completes my re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Lee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one brief question for you. And could we have on our screens the -- Madam Registrar, perhaps you could assist me, the first of the three photographs that were marked by the witness and were separated.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was P417, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P417. If you would give me one second to phrase my question, Mr. Kapetanovic. Yes, could I ask you the following: Do I understand you well that you were playing approximately where this greenish shed is at the end of the street which you marked? You were playing there, and it's there where you heard the first shell being fired, which made you run back home. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you were asked how far you ran approximately when you heard that shell up till the moment where the shell landed and you were hit by that shell. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My answer was 10 to 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I look at this photographs, I have some difficulty with your estimate that it would be only 10 or 15 metres, because it seems to be far more to me; because, first, to cross the street from the shed, from the green shed, and then it seems that it was quite a bit more. Would you agree with me, or ... because 15 metres, as far as I am able to deduce from this picture, would certainly -- not any closer than where this man walks.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you're saying. You mean to say that I ran and -- for more than 15 metres?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least. I -- looking at this photograph, I would not exclude that the distance would have been more than the 10 or more metres you told us.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat what you said? I'm afraid I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wondered whether the distance you ran, starting at the shed where you were sleighing, whether, when you were hit, whether you had not yet covered more metres than the 10 or 15 you told us.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. My estimate was 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any further questions? If not, Mr. Kapetanovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you. I can imagine that it may not have been easy for you to have been taken back to the incident you testified about. We wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the next witness is called, I need to make a submission to the Chamber. I can do that either before or after the break, whichever pleases the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if you can do it in two or three minutes then we will then take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, this submission relates to the next witness, Richard Mole. Several weeks ago, Ms. Hochhauser brought to my attention a document that she came across in her final preparations to lead the evidence of this witness. It was her opinion that the document was of a type that we were obliged to disclose under Rule 68(i). After studying the document considering that in the context of this case, the case against Mr. Mladic, I shared her opinion and made the legal determination that our obligations under Rule 68(i) did require us to disclose the document. The document is identified by ERN number R0155267 to R0155270. It is a document of four pages, one being a fax cover and a three-page memo. It was provided to the OTP by an organisation pursuant to Rule 70. Once the determination was made that disclosure was required, we requested from the provider permission to disclose the document to Mr. Mladic. We are still discussing this request with the provider but we're unfortunately unable to secure permission to disclose it prior to today, the date of the witness's evidence. When it became clear that the hurricane over the eastern seaboard would make it impossible to get this permission, I brought it to the attention of both Mr. Lukic and Mr. Nilsson, the Chamber's Senior Legal Officer. I proposed to Mr. Lukic that we proceed with the evidence of Mr. Mole and that I would disclose the document as soon as we received permission to do so. Further, I gave an undertaking that I would not oppose any application by the Mladic Defence to recall the witness should it deem that it is necessary to question the witness about the document. The matter has been raised with Mr. Mole and he appreciates and accepts that he may be required to return to The Hague. If that is an acceptable way of proceeding, Your Honour, the Prosecution would be prepared to call Mr. Mole at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that the Defence does not disagree with proceeding as you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm handling the witness. Mr. Lukic did advise me of this yesterday, and I agreed with him this appeared to be a reasonable means of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll proceed as suggested by Mr. Groome. But we'll first take a break, and we'll resume at a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, unless there are any preliminaries, I would like to -- the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, good afternoon. As the witness is being brought in, I would just like to place on the record the adjudicated fact on which the Prosecution relied in redacting the proposed 92 ter statement and in deciding not to elicit certain information during examination. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I inform the Prosecution and the parties that leave to reply to the response to the 92 ter motion is granted. Good afternoon, Mr. Mole.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is handed out to you now. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mole. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, there was also a request for adding documents to the 65 ter list. Whenever it comes to tendering of any of the documents, the Chamber will understand this as including a decision on adding the document to the 65 ter list. So we come to that once the document is dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mole, you will first be examined, although not for a very long time today, for only 20 minutes, by Ms. Hochhauser. Ms. Hochhauser is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel. Can you please state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: My name is Richard Mole.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And are you currently employed, Colonel Mole?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: I am. I'm self-employed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I take it then that you are retired from any military service?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: I retired in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And what was the last position you held before retiring?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: I was the Chief of Staff in a unit in Germany from whence I went to Bosnia on the UN attachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I have just been reminded by Ms. Stewart to myself and I'll advise you as well that we need to pause between our questions and answers since we're speaking in the same language. Give a little time for the translators. Now, Colonel Mole, you have previously provided statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in September 1997 and April 2002; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: You also previously testified in the cases against both Stanislav Galic and Radovan Karadzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In preparation for your testimony in the Karadzic case, you signed amalgamated statement on 7th of May, 2010, which amalgamated relevant portions of your two previous statements and the testimony in the Galic case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could please ask the usher to place 65 ter 28455 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, Colonel, do you recognise the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is that the amalgamated statement we just discussed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, have you had the opportunity to review this statement again before testifying here today?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: On 17 August 2010 during your testimony in the Karadzic case, in -- in that case as transcript page 5805 to 5806, you made a correction to your amalgamated statement at paragraph 12 in which you stated that the sentence as it reads in the written document which says, "There were approximately seven manned observation posts on each side" should in fact read as follows:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which paragraph, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, it's at paragraph 12. And I believe this information, this correction was previously provided to the Chamber and Defence via e-mail.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So at paragraph 12 should correctly read: "With respect to the monitoring of weapons, there were 14 observation posts. At the end of October 1992, ten were on the Lima side and four on the Papa side. By the end of November 1992, there were 11 on the Lima side and three on the Papa side, and this remained the case until my departure." Now, what I've just read, is that a correction to your amalgamated statement that you would still make today?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And other than that correction, is the statement that's on the monitor in front of you, the amalgamated statement, both accurate and truthful?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today that you were asked when you provided the information contained in this statement, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may I now tender 65 ter 28455, the amalgamated statement, into evidence. I see my colleague is standing, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- Mr. Registrar. We've changed during the last session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It becomes Exhibit P421, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P421 is admitted into evidence. You may proceed, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would also like to tender the associated exhibits into evidence. As Your Honours will note from the chart provided one of the associated exhibits is already in evidence as P00300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can we take them one by one --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections to anyone of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we go through them one by one. 65 ter 10775.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P422, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. P10776.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P423, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 10777.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P424, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 10778.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P425, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 65 ter 10787.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P426, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 65 ter 15875.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P427, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Next one is 15895.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P428, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Last one, 19543.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P429, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is also admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this time, with the Court's permission, I will read a brief summary of just the written evidence contained in Mr. Mole's statement. Lieutenant-Colonel Richard Mole served in the British Army for over 20 years prior to his assignment to the former Yugoslavia as a United Nations Military Observer. After initial posts in Croatia and in Belgrade, Colonel Mole was posted to Sarajevo as a Senior Military Observer and served there from 16 September 1992 until 26 December 1992. In Sarajevo, Colonel Mole was in charge of approximately 60 United Nations Military Observers positioned on both sides of the confrontation line with a mandate to, among observer things, monitor and report on heavy weapons activity. Colonel Mole's written evidence describes the intense shelling in Sarajevo and the intense psychological pressure which resulted for the city's citizens. He describes indiscriminate and untargeted shelling of the city by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and how he and his monitors sought explanations from that corps' commanders and received explanations which showed no military justification for the shelling. Colonel Mole frequently met with the SRK commander, General Galic, and observed the regular and effective chain of command of Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. He also protested the indiscriminate shelling to members of that corps and to its command and in his evidence states that Galic threatened to shell Sarajevo city if events elsewhere did not transpire in the favour of the Bosnian Serbs. Colonel Mole came to view the Bosnian Serb strategy in Sarajevo as a policy of containment in that their use of force was not justified by military necessity but rather by an effort to apply pressure to the city in order to achieve their aims. Your Honour, that concludes my summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. If you have any further questions for the witness, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Mole, as you know the Chamber is already in position of the statement which is now in evidence and has carefully reviewed it so that our time in court will be spent clarifying a few things from your statement and discussing topics that are not addressed in it. First, I'd like to define a few terms that you say use in your statement. You refer throughout it to the Lima and Papa sides. Can you just tell us which is Lima and which is Papa?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: The Papa side was that designated applied to the Presidency side within the city of Sarajevo. The Lima side was designated UNMOs outside the city, hosted by the SRK.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: You used in your statement the term increp, i-n-c-r-e-p. Can you tell us what is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: It is a short word for instant report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And also shootrep?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: Similarly it's a short word for shoot report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And sitrep is that --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: Situation report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you tell us just a brief description of what is recorded in each of those three reports, what the differences are?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: A situation report would be a report that I would probably assemble using information and data that I had collected for submission up my chain of command. A shootrep would be a report that was completed on a pro forma, as was an incident report, completed on a pro forma. The shootrep would record outgoing rounds from weapons that UN Military Observers were next to or nearby or could observe. The increp or incident report would be a reciprocal report except that it would report incoming fire that, again, was observed by United Nations Military Observers.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now you told us -- you describe it as a pro forma. Is that meaning a standardised form that was used for all the reporters?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: Yes. There was a form which we trained the individual UN Military Observers to use. The aim of giving them a standard form was to facilitate reading serials over a radio without having to go through detailed explanation. I feel sure that we'll probably come onto the detail of that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might interrupt, I'm sorry. Just for my edification, Colonel, when you say a shootrep, I beg your pardon. When you talk of an outgoing fire from weapons that the United Nations Military Observers were next to or nearby or could observe, I'm not quite sure I understand what -- who was actually shooting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question, sir, was relating to the form. I didn't say who was or wasn't shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. It could be either side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Colonel Mole, just to follow up on that for a moment. The UN monitor who was filling out the form, can you give us an example of where they would be -- where one might be standing when filling out a shootrep? Where they might be positioned.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: Indeed. As the name of the report suggests, it is a weapon that is actually being fired, so clearly a UN Military Observer would have to be in the proximity of that weapon to be able to observe it. So for the majority of the shootreps which were expedited, most of them would be on the Lima side, since that was where most heavy weapons were. So if I may give an example.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: That, on a gun site where UN Military Observers were co-located with that gun site, if the commander of the gun decided on a fire mission once the rounds were leaving the weapons, it would invoke a shootrep. That shootrep would then be filled out filling in the all the various serials within that form to give as much information as possible so that that could then be reported to myself and up the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, in paragraphs 12 through 14 of your statement you talk about observation posts and weapon sights at the two different types of locations that you were monitoring. And I think you have just begun to give an example of perhaps a weapon sight. Can you tell us the difference, please, between observation posts and weapons sights. What are the two different types of locations that you're monitoring?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE
utterances.text: I think it's important at this stage to put the two into perspective. The airport agreement of 1992 initiated weapon collection points, and that was invoked on both sides. The detail of the agreement included, or was meant to include, the collection of weapons so that they then wouldn't be used. Now that isn't what transpired. What happened was we had UN Military Observers who were allocated to weapons sights but the weapons were still obviously in use. Now that applied to both sides, the Presidency side and the Serb side. So, as a consequence, we deployed UN Military Observers to Papa and Lima, as I've already explained. Disposition of weapons on both sides was at variance. Most of the heavy weapons were held by the Serb side. Some were held by the Presidency side. Now, at this juncture I must point out that when I talk of the Presidency side, I speak of those weapons within Sarajevo, within the city itself. They didn't have a large number of weapons within the Presidency side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's a problem with the interpretation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Interpretation seems to be problematic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the clock seems to be problematic as well at this moment because we usually finish at quarter past 2.00. It is quarter past 2.00 now so we have a whole night to repair any other technical problems. Mr. Mole, we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. But I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with or communicate in any other way with whomever about your testimony, either the -- the testimony given today or testimony still to be given in tomorrow or even the day after tomorrow. So we'd like to see you back, and I invite you to follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 1st of November, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 1st day of November, 2012, at 9.30 a.m.
